title: S5 task quarantine never fires for wave lanes — items are never claimed to processing/, so FAIL releases bump no failure_count
evidence: Batch-14: workspace-hygiene-s5-wiring-shadow-default failed its cycle FOUR times (1137 agent-graded FAIL, 1139 agent-graded FAIL, 1142 EGPS red, 1143 agent-graded FAIL) and was re-dispatched every wave with failure_count never incremented — .evolve/inbox/processing/ holds only stale cycle-411/416/425 dirs, so ReleaseCycleProcessingWithQuarantine (the ONLY bumpFailureCount caller, inboxmover.go:675) iterates an empty processing/cycle-N/ and quarantine ceilings (ADR-0072 S5 task_retry_ceiling) are structurally unreachable for fleet-dispatched work. The identical-fingerprint breaker's false halt MASKED this: it stopped the batch before the grind became obvious. Wave lanes keep items in inbox root (per-id Promote on ship covers the SUCCESS path only).
notes: Fix the LIFECYCLE, not the counter: either (a) wave dispatch Claims each lane-scope id into processing/cycle-N at launch (freshness gate already excludes in-flight ids within a wave; cross-wave claims make consumption/failure accounting transactional — the forensics rule 'item-consumption must be transactional with landing'), with release-on-FAIL walking the SAME claim; or (b) keep root-resident items but route the FAIL path through a per-id failure_count bump keyed by lane-scope ids (smaller, but leaves two lifecycle models alive — option (a) preferred per never_duplicate_centralize). Interacts with lane MENUS (PR #366): only ids triage COMMITTED should bump on FAIL, not the whole menu.
acceptance: RED first: a wave lane whose cycle FAILs leaves its committed item with failure_count+1; at task_retry_ceiling the item moves to quarantine and is not re-seeded.
Menu semantics: unworked menu ids (not committed by triage) neither bump nor quarantine.
Success path unchanged: per-id Promote to processed/ still works from inbox root or processing/.
cd go && go test -race ./internal/inboxmover/... ./cmd/evolve/... N/N PASS.
